sections.h2: How do I search Leon County, Texas property records?
sections.html:
Deed and official records for Leon County are online, and the County Clerk's office in Centerville also keeps eight public search stations. The clerk's page says the deed and official records on those stations reach back to 1828, probate to 1848, marriage records to 1885, and criminal records from 1995, with plats available too.

Records on the Leon County Clerk's public search stations
Record setYears the clerk's page lists
Deed and official records1828 forward

PlatsAvailable on the stations

The office is on the first floor at 155 North Cass Street, Centerville, TX 75833. Staff will show visitors how to use the indexes, and anyone may do their own research. The page sets a few house rules worth knowing before a trip:

  • Photography of the large Tobin maps and of images on the public stations is prohibited, and flash photography is not allowed.
  • Removing a document, page or volume from the office is a state jail felony under Penal Code 32.47.
  • The clerk gives no legal advice, does not decide who owns surface or mineral rights, and does not run lien searches.
  • Under Attorney General Opinion WW-607, the clerk has no duty to search the records and guarantee they are correct.

sections.h2: What are the Leon County Clerk's hours, recording fee and filing options?
sections.html:
The clerk's office is open Monday through Friday from 7:45 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., including the lunch hour, but recording stops at 4 p.m. A document received after 4 p.m. is recorded the next business day. Cash, checks and major credit cards are accepted.

The page lists a recording fee of $15 for the first page and $4 for each additional page of an instrument, under a fee schedule that took effect January 1, 2024. Companies that handle electronic filing into the official records are named on the page: Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Fees can change, so ask the office for the current schedule before sending payment.

Which deputy handles what also matters. The chief deputy's desk covers general recording and indexing and copy requests. Probate and civil filings, marriage licenses, and birth and death records each go through different staff, with separate options on the phone menu.

sections.h2: What does Texas require before a Leon County deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
Texas allows a conveyance of real property to be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged, or sworn before two witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). A notary, county clerk, district clerk or county court judge may take the acknowledgment.

The 2023 county clerk manual says the clerk records general warranty deeds, special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds and tax deeds, along with releases of deeds of trust, affidavits and contracts of sale. It lists a statutory base fee of $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, plus other clerk charges. A missing grantee mailing address may add $25. Leon County's own posted rate is the one to use when you file.

A deed cannot add heirs after the fact. When an owner has died, the clerk manual points to an executor's deed for an administered estate, a court order with the will for a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship when nothing else is available.

sections.h2: What is Leon County like for a homeowner or seller?
sections.html:
Leon County is a rural county east of Waco along Interstate 45, between Dallas and Houston. The Census Bureau estimates 16,894 residents on July 1, 2025, up 7.2 percent from the April 2020 base. It reports 9,255 housing units, 6,741 households and a land area of 1,073.16 square miles.

For 2020 to 2024, the owner-occupied rate is 76.6 percent and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $186,400. Median monthly owner costs run $1,557 with a mortgage and $502 without one. Median gross rent is $907, and the mean trip to work takes 29.3 minutes. About 27.9 percent of residents are 65 or older.

The Handbook of Texas notes that the county was formed from Robertson County in 1846, that Centerville became county seat in 1851 after first seat Leona, and that Buffalo is the largest community. Jewett, Normangee, Oakwood and Marquez are other towns. U.S. Highway 79 crosses east to west, the Trinity River forms the eastern boundary, and Lake Limestone sits in the northwest corner. Oil and gas, agribusiness and lumber are described as key parts of the economy.

sections.h2: Who handles Leon County values and tax bills?
sections.html:
The Leon Central Appraisal District sets values, and the county tax assessor-collector sends the bills. The county's assessor-collector page tells owners to take changes to a tax account or questions about appraised value to the appraisal district at 141 W. St. Mary's, Centerville, TX 75833, telephone 903-536-2252.

The same page lists delinquent tax attorneys by taxing unit. One law firm in Waco is named for the county, a different firm in Corsicana for Normangee ISD, and a third firm in Tyler for Buffalo ISD, the City of Marquez and Oakwood ISD. If a notice from a collection firm arrives, the unit that sent it determines which firm applies.

Statewide, values are set as of January 1, bills go out in October, and January 31 is the last day to pay without penalty. A lien for each year's tax attaches on January 1, so a Leon County house carries that year's tax with it into a sale. See our Leon County property tax guide for the county tax office.

sections.h2: What title problems turn up in the Leon County records?
sections.html:
A probate case never opened is the common one in a county where about 28 percent of residents are 65 or older. If a parent's name is still the last owner on the deed, the file needs a legal path to the heirs.

  • A will must generally be probated within four years of death, though a court can accept a later filing for an acceptable reason.
  • A small estate affidavit requires no will, no pending administration, assets of $75,000 or less excluding homestead and exempt property, and every heir's agreement. Two disinterested witnesses swear to it and at least 30 days must have passed since death.
  • A muniment of title lets a will serve as proof of ownership when the only debts are real estate liens.
  • An affidavit of heirship is filed with the Leon County Clerk, though nothing requires a buyer or lender to rely on it.

Inherited homestead property can also qualify for a residence exemption, but heirs not named on a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Leon County house with a title or lien problem?
sections.html: Yes. A buyer paying cash can purchase as-is, and the title company clears recorded items at closing where the payoff can be documented. If you have found an unreleased mortgage, a probate gap or a back tax bill in the Leon County records, send us the details and we will explain the likely route to closing.

faqs.q: What time does the Leon County Clerk stop recording documents?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 4 p.m., although the office stays open until 4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday. Anything received after 4 p.m. is recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: How much does the Leon County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The clerk's page lists $15 for the first page and $4 for each additional page of an instrument. The fee schedule took effect January 1, 2024, so confirm the amount with the office when you file.

faqs.q: Are Leon County deed records available online?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk says deed and official records are online, and the same records back to 1828 can be viewed on public stations in the Centerville office.

faqs.q: Will the Leon County Clerk tell me who owns the minerals?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's page says staff cannot determine surface or mineral ownership or perform lien searches. A title company or attorney handles that work.

faqs.q: Where do I contest a Leon County appraisal?
faqs.a: Contact the Leon Central Appraisal District at 903-536-2252. A protest to the appraisal review board is generally due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice of value is delivered, whichever is later.
